_comment: O'Mara Constructions Pty Ltd, Mulgrave NSW (near Windsor). Hand-written 2026-09-24 from https://www.omara.com.au because `npm run new` is broken in this container (see HANDOVER.md). I read every page with curl. Every specific fact on the page is quoted in _source.claimSources with its URL, or comes from data/google_reviews_top25.json. Google has only 2 reviews, one with no text, so the proof leans on facts from their own site (founder's OAM and MBA presidency, MBA membership since 1968, the Sydney 2000 Olympic Village homes, flame-zone and sloping-site work). The builders preset's process, FAQ and responsePromise describe a generic builder and would be invented claims here, so all three are fully overridden with O'Mara's own published process and answers. Reviews: only one Google review has text. It appears once, in the reviews section. There's no pull quote, so the same words don't show twice.
tagline: Custom homes, second storeys and hard-site builds across the Hawkesbury, the Hills and the Blue Mountains. Family owned since 1964.

phone._comment: Luke's mobile, which their site gives as the number to 'Call & speak to the builder direct'. I tried labelling it '0419 979 804 · Luke's mobile' in the display field, but the longer text squashed the header logo on a phone (a Best Practices aspect-ratio fail). So the label is in the responsePromise line directly under the hero call button instead. The office landline (02) 4577 4912 (matches Google) is in that line and in the enquiry intro.

brand._comment: Accent is the timber of the roof-truss 'A' in their own logo, brightened so it reads as a button on the dark theme. Accent2 is the pale blue of the 'R' in the same logo. Neither is a published brand colour.

I made the white background transparent and cropped off the 'Proudly Family Owned' tagline under it (dark grey text that would be unreadable on the dark header). The saw-blade O, ruler M, truss A, R and square-and-compass A wordmark is unchanged. Original kept as assets/logo-omara-original.jpg.

copy.title: O'Mara Constructions: Custom Home Builders, Hawkesbury, Hills & Blue Mountains
copy.description: Family-owned custom home builders since 1964, based at Mulgrave near Windsor. Second storey additions, custom new homes, bushfire and sloping-site homes, renovations. Call Luke O'Mara direct.
copy.headline:
Any block.
Any design.
Since 1964.
copy.sub: Steep bush blocks, flame zones, flood-affected land and heritage homes. Three generations of our family have built custom homes and second storeys on the sites other builders won't touch.
copy.heroSecondarySms: Or text Luke a photo of the block
copy.statementBody: Most homes in bushfire country sit on a slope, where a standard slab, brick veneer and tiled roof won't work or costs far too much. We build pole homes and Spantec steel floors on steep ground, bushfire homes from BAL 12.5 right up to flame zone, and homes on flood-affected, narrow and remote blocks. We've lived in the Hawkesbury all our lives, and we've seen firsthand what a bushfire does to a house.
copy.servicesIntro: No standard designs and no project-home rules. Bring your own plans for a price, or get help drawing a concept. You can use any materials from any supplier.
copy.apertureLine: Every one of our carpenters works for us full time, from framing to fix-out joinery.
copy.workIntro: Bushfire homes by the river and in the mountains, heritage renovations, and the bathrooms inside them.
copy.processIntro: Our advice: don't sign a building contract until council has approved the plans and your builder is ready to start.
copy.recognitionIntro: Over 60 years of standing in the industry, and the cover that protects your build.
copy.areasIntro: We're based at Mulgrave near Windsor, with crews across western Sydney. Our rates are the same in every area, with no extra charge for travel. These are suburbs where we've built.
copy.enquireIntro: Send the address, what you want to build and a rough budget. Luke can usually check the site on Street View before he calls you back. Or ring the office on (02) 4577 4912.

process.detail: He can usually look up the address on Street View while you're on the phone and tell you straight away whether, say, a second storey will work. If not, he'll visit the site. There's no fee for this.
A basic plan drawn to scale, not full council drawings. It starts with a written brief: your budget, a must list, a don't list and a wish list.
We price the concept at no cost. Every quote is specific to your site, with all site costs included and no hidden costs. We can price alternative materials or methods too.
Council approval comes first, and we can lodge it for you at no fee. Then you sign the MBA BC4 fixed price contract, the HBCF cover goes in and we start building.

reviews.name: Lauran Trevena
reviews.text: Great honest and friendly builder. Provides great work and a great price.

faq.q: Can we stay in the house during a second storey addition?
faq.a: Most clients do. The crew comes in via the scaffold and through the roof, not your front door. To be honest, we'll likely kill your grass storing materials and we'll make noise early in the morning. But we clean up daily and keep a safe, secure way into your home.

faq.q: Is my house strong enough to build on top of?
faq.a: Most homes are, but a builder should check. Homes sitting on brick piers only, or in very poor condition, may not suit. Call Luke with the address. He can usually tell from Street View straight away, or he'll come out to the site.

faq.q: Can you build on a bushfire-prone or steep block?
faq.a: Yes. We build from BAL 12.5 right through to flame zone, and on steep ground we use pole homes and Spantec steel floor systems. Flame zone adds real cost, so it pays to plan for it at the concept stage rather than after.

faq.q: Can I supply some of the materials myself?
faq.a: Yes. There are no restrictions on suppliers, and owners can supply items like tiles, bathroom fittings or appliances directly. Ask first how it affects insurance, warranties and the construction program.

faq.q: Do you charge extra to travel?
faq.a: No. Our rates are the same for every area, whether you're building at Pitt Town, Penrith or Katoomba.
The Master Builders Association BC4 fixed price building contract, or an MBA NSW cost plus contract. Don't sign any building contract until council approval is in hand.
